query_text: Should we rely on self-driving cars for transportation?

action.query: NHTSA automated vehicles safety self driving cars 2025 2026
queries: NHTSA automated vehicles safety self driving cars 2025 2026
IIHS partial automation safeguards ratings self driving 2024
Waymo safety data autonomous vehicle crashes 2025

annotations.title: Waymo recalls more than 1,200 automated vehicles after minor crashes - Los Angeles Times

content.text:
**Not yet as a universal replacement—but yes, cautiously, in limited settings.**

Self-driving cars can be useful transportation **when they operate in a constrained, well-tested service area**—for example, a robotaxi service in mapped urban zones, good weather, and with clear company/regulatory oversight. But we should **not fully rely on them everywhere** yet, especially for rural roads, severe weather, construction zones, emergency situations, or places where the system has not been validated.

A practical stance:

- **Use them where they’re proven and regulated.** Some autonomous ride-hailing services have accumulated large numbers of driverless miles and report lower crash rates than human-driver benchmarks in their operating areas, but those results are specific to those fleets, cities, and conditions. ([waymo.com](https://waymo.com/safety/impact/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Do not confuse driver-assistance with self-driving.** Most cars consumers can buy today with “Autopilot,” “Full Self-Driving,” lane-centering, or adaptive cruise control are still **partial automation** and require an attentive human driver. NHTSA says true automated driving systems are not generally something you can buy and use as a personal car today. ([nhtsa.gov](https://www.nhtsa.gov/vehicle-safety/automated-vehicles-safety?utm_source=openai))  
- **Safety safeguards still need work.** IIHS found in its partial-automation safeguard ratings that most systems had inadequate protections against driver inattention or misuse, and emphasized that partial automation is not self-driving. ([iihs.org](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/partial-automation-safeguards?ftag=YHF4eb9d17&utm_source=openai))  
- **Expect failures and edge cases.** Even leading robotaxi systems have had recalls, investigations, or problematic incidents involving unusual traffic situations, school buses, power outages, or infrastructure issues. That does not mean the technology is hopeless; it means society should deploy it gradually and with accountability. ([latimes.com](https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2025-05-14/waymo-recalls-more-than-1-200-automated-vehicles-after-minor-crashes?utm_source=openai))  

**Bottom line:** We should rely on self-driving cars **as one transportation option**, not as the backbone of transportation yet. The best policy is phased adoption: allow autonomous vehicles in areas where data show they are safe, require transparent crash reporting and independent audits, keep strong human-driver safeguards for partial automation, and preserve alternatives like public transit, walking, biking, taxis, and human-driven vehicles.
